Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education: Graduate of an Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredited College or School of Pharmacy with a baccalaureate degree in pharmacy (BS Pharmacy) and/or a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree.

Graduates of foreign pharmacy degree programs meet the educational requirement if the graduate is able to provide proof of achieving the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Commission (FPGEC) Certification, which includes passing the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Equivalency Examination (FPGEE) and the Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TEOFL iBT).

Licensure: Full, current and unrestricted license to practice pharmacy in a State, Territory, Commonwealth of the United States (i.e., Puerto Rico), or the District of Columbia. The pharmacist must maintain current registration if this is a requirement for maintaining full, current, and unrestricted licensure.

A pharmacist who has, or has ever had, any license(s) revoked, suspended, denied, restricted, limited, or issued/placed in a probationary status may be appointed only in accordance with the provisions in VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section B, paragraph 16.

English Language Proficiency: Pharmacists must be proficient in spoken and written English as required by 38 U.S.C. 7402(d), and 7407(d). Grade Determinations: GS-13 Experience: In addition to the GS-12 requirements, must have 1 year of experience equivalent to the next lower grade level.

Assignments: Candidates at this grade level are to be in one of the assignments listed below.

For all assignments above the full performance level, the higher level duties must consist of significant scope, administrative independence, complexity (difficulty) and range of variety as described in this standard at the specified grade level and be performed by the incumbent at least 25% of the time.

Facility Program Manager: Manages all aspects of a distinct program to include policy development, quality resources and specialty functions unique to the program to optimize cost effectiveness (budget) and patient outcomes.

Coordinates a single program area of a complex pharmacy operation, or multiple program areas within a facility to develop, organize, manage, and control complex pharmacy programs. Develops, organizes, coordinates and manages 6 single or multiple program areas within the medical facility; this may include a single program area at multiple facilities.

The Program Manager title is reserved for those individuals who have one or more of the following: supervisory responsibilities for various sections within Pharmacy Service; a complex program requiring coordination of multiple locations such as medical center care facilities, Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), rural health, telemedicine, etc; specialized areas of a complex nature such as nuclear pharmacy, quality assurance, pharmacy informatics, clinical applications coordinator, Home Based Primary Care, pharmacoeconomist or liaison pharmacist duties requiring the coordination of processes with other medical facilities or VISNs.

Pharmacists assigned to this position must demonstrate the following KSAs: Ability to communicate orally and in writing to persuade and influence clinical and management decisions. Expert understanding of regulatory and quality standards for their program area.

Ability to solve problems, coordinate and organize responsibilities to maximize outcomes in their program area or area of clinical expertise. Expert knowledge of a specialized area of clinical pharmacy practice or specialty area of pharmacy.

Advanced skill in monitoring and assessing the outcome of drug therapies, including physical assessment and interpretation of laboratory and other diagnostic parameters. Preferred Experience: Experience with transitioning to new electronic health records is preferred.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Grandfathering Provision: All licensed pharmacists employed in VHA in this occupation on the effective date of this qualification standard are considered to have met all qualification requirements for the title, series and grade held, including positive education and licensure/certification/registration that are part of the basic requirements of the occupation.

For employees who do not meet all the basic requirements required in this standard, but who met the qualifications applicable to the position at the time they were appointed to it, the following provisions apply: Employees grandfathered into the GS-660 occupational series may be reassigned, promoted up to and including the full performance (journey) level, or changed to lower grade within the occupation, but may not be promoted beyond the journey level or placed in supervisory or managerial positions.

Employees who are appointed on a temporary basis prior to the effective date of the qualification standard may not have their temporary appointment extended or be reappointed, on a temporary or permanent basis, until they fully meet the basic requirements of the standard.

Employees initially grandfathered into this occupation, who subsequently obtain additional education and/or licensure/certification/registration, that meet all the basic requirements of this qualification standard must maintain the required credentials as a condition of employment in the occupation.

If a licensed pharmacist who was retained under this provision leaves the occupation, the employee loses protected status and must meet the full VA qualification standard requirements in effect at the time of reentry to the occupation.

Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. This position is above the full performance level. Physical Requirements: Must be able to distinguish basic colors.

For the GS-11: To meet the Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology (IT) Management Series (2210), you must possess: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations.

Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.

Technical Competence - Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues.

AND Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled.

Such experience is typically gained in the IT field or through the performance of work where the primary concern is IT. GS-11 Specialized experience: You must possess one-year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-9 level.

Specialized experience is defined as applying analytical methods and practices sufficient to conduct analyses and recommend resolution of complex issues affecting the Electronic Health Record (EHR) deployment and remediation of high risk IT processes related to program control and management.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religions; spiritual; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Hey there!
We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.
Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.
Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.
Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?
To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience?
Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
Team context
User Operations sits within Fever's broader User Support organization. User Operations is the strategic/enablement layer behind the operating User support structure, organized around three areas: AI integration, Systems, and Data.
Within Data, we focus on continuous improvement. We don't just maintain information that's useful and relevant to stakeholders inside and outside the department, we translate that data into concrete initiatives that let us keep questioning and improving how we work.

We're looking for a Project Manager with a strong analytics backbone. This isn't a "build the dashboard and move on", we need someone who can go from constructing the data (dashboards, reporting, automations) to understanding what it actually means for the business, so they can help management make consistently data-driven decisions.
Projects will range from a variety of stakeholders, such as, providing user support with operating actionable metrics, giving partners visibility into how their events are performing or helping on app developments that directly shape the user experience.

Analytics (70% weight)
2-4 years of experience in data/analytics (analyst, data PM, BI, ops analytics). A relevant Master's or further training in the field is a plus.
Comfortable building and maintaining dashboards in tools like Metabase, Looker, or similar.
Scripting/automation experience.
Project management & structure (30% weight)
Demonstrated ability to run a project end-to-end.
Organized, structured, and comfortable prioritizing your own workload.
You default to improving things, not just maintaining them. When you spot something inefficient, you fix it or raise it, you don't leave it for later.
Comfortable communicating with both technical (central Data team) and non-technical (support ops) stakeholders.
Not required today, but a plus: some early signs of enjoying explaining things to others or helping people grow. This role is expected to evolve into managing a team member over time, no prior people-management experience needed.
Languages & location
Full professional fluency in both English and Spanish, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Based in Madrid or willing to relocate to Madrid

Job Title: Senior Clinical Project Manager, Oncology, IQVIA Biotech
Job Location: Kirkland, Quebec, Canada
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Full-time

IQVIA Biotech is a full-service CRO purpose-built to serve biotech sponsors. With over 25 years of experience, we offer agile, therapeutically aligned solutions and trusted partnerships that help bring breakthrough treatments to patients faster.
We are seeking a Senior Clinical Project Manager with proven experience in Oncologyclinical trials to join IQVIA Biotech. This role is ideal for a seasoned project management professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is passionate about advancing therapies in the Immuno-Oncology space. You will leverage your expertise to lead complex, multi-regional studies and ensure operational excellence while building strong client relationships.

As a Senior Clinical Project Manager at IQVIA Biotech, you’ll play a critical role in accelerating the delivery of clinical trials and improving patient lives by bringing new therapies to market faster. You will lead core project teams, ensuring successful execution of clinical studies in alignment with contractual requirements, SOPs, and regulatory standards. This role combines strategic leadership, operational excellence, and customer engagement to deliver high-quality results.

Lead bid defense presentations and contribute to study strategy development.
Develop and implement integrated study management plans.
Oversee planning and execution of medium to large, multi-regional clinical studies, ensuring speed, quality, and cost optimization.
Serve as the primary point of contact for clients, fostering strong relationships and customer satisfaction.
Build and lead cross-functional teams, driving collaboration and milestone achievement.
Monitor project progress, manage risks, and resolve issues proactively.
Ensure compliance with ICH GCP, local regulations, and company processes.
Manage project financials, including forecasting, scope changes, and revenue acceleration opportunities.
Mentor and support team members, promoting continuous improvement and knowledge sharing.

Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences or related field.
7+ years of clinical research experience, including 4+ years in project management.
Strong knowledge of clinical trial conduct, regulatory requirements, and therapeutic areas.
Excellent leadership, communication, and negotiation skills.
Proven ability to manage complex projects across geographies and functions.
Proficiency in MS Office and project management tools.

At CesiumAstro , we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization.

If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team.
We are looking to add a Senior Program Manager to our team. If you enjoy working in a startup environment and managing multiple fast paced projects at once, we would like to hear from you.
In this position, you will be responsible for program performance and day-to-day execution for a large customer subsystem or a small to medium sized payload, including concept development, implementation, production, modification, integration and test, and delivery. You will be the single point of contact for customer interactions including program management reviews, customer bi-weekly reviews, and major program reviews. This position is expected to be able to manage multiple customers.
This position works collaboratively with all functional organizations at CesiumAstro to ensure the success of the program using risk -bsaed decision making in guiding decisions to meet program objectives. A successful candidate understands how to effectively use program and engineering metrics to make data driven decisions. You will serve as the primary program leader for all activities, with responsibilities for cost, schedule, and adherence to technical performance requirements.
The Senior Program Manager will establish program management baselines (integrated master plans and resource loaded schedules) to task the team, measures program performance, and monitors progress to generate latest revised estimates and estimates to completion. The Senior Program Manager will provide these inputs to customers, CesiumAstro leadership, and internal finance teams for revenue recognition.
This position will assist the Director of Programs in improving standard processes, and implementing best practices for consistency across the Space Payloads portfolio of programs. As a senior member of the program team, you may help in hiring and mentorship of program engineers.

Minimum of 12-15 years of Program Management or Subcontract Management Experience.
Bachelor of Science (BS) or Master of Science (MS) degree in a relevant engineering field (Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, etc.) from an accredited university or institution.
Experience in the aerospace industry as a system or design engineer.
Develop and coordinate program requirements across product lines and with multiple subcontractors
Familiarity with RF, communication, or satellite systems.
Experience managing cross functional and decentralized teams.

Wollen Sie im Projekt für diesen zukünftigen Grossbetrieb unter Berücksichtigung der kantonalen Vorgaben (Nachhaltigkeit, rechtliche und formale Vorgaben) aktiv mitgestalten und einen wesentlichen Beitrag zur Umsetzung für einen adäquaten Justizvollzug leisten? Der Wettbewerb zum Neubauprojekt ist im Gange, die Zuschlagsverfügung zur Ausführung für Mitte 2028 geplant und die Bewilligung des Ausführungskredites durch den Grossen Rat wird im Sommer 2029 erwartet.
Mit dem Neubau für den geschlossenen Männervollzug soll die heutige offene Justizvollzugsanstalt (JVA) Witzwil um einen geschlossenen Betrieb mit 200 Vollzugsplätzen erweitert werden. Neu soll die JVA Witzwil rund 400 Vollzugsplätze in den Regimen offenen und geschlossenen Männervollzug, Untersuchungshaft sowie Administrativhaft anbieten. Damit würde das Konzept \ realisiert.
Mit der Perspektive als zukünftiges Geschäftsleitungsmitglied der JVA Witzwil -- Bereich Infrastruktur (ca. ab Mitte 2029) übernehmen Sie bereits heute die nutzerseitige Betriebsprojektleitung für weitere Infrastrukturprojekte in Witzwil. Bis zum Übertritt in die Organisationsstruktur der JVA Witzwil werden Ihnen weitere Projekt(leitungs)aufgaben für amtsweite Vorhaben anvertraut.
**Ihre Aufgaben**
* Betriebsprojektleitung Neubau JVA Witzwil gemäss Pflichtenheft und Projekthandbuch
* Gegenüber Bauherrschaft, internen Anspruchsgruppen und Dritten die Interessen wahrnehmen für den Justizvollzug des Kantons Bern und die JVA Witzwil dies in Bezug auf Planung und Realisierung einer effizienten, nachhaltigen, modernen und störungsfreien Objektbewirtschaftung sowie für den Betrieb der zukünftigen technischen und organisatorischen Strukturen
* Eine geeignete Betriebsorganisation (interne und externe Ressourcen) aufbauen
* Das Projekt in den Bereichen Sicherheitstechnik / Facility Management / Instandhaltung / Heizung, Lüftung, Klimatisierung, Kälte, Sanitär und Elektro (HLKKSE) / Mess-, Steuerungs- und Regelungstechnik (MSRL) / Building Information Modeling (BIM) begleiten
* Die zukünftigen Betriebsstrukturen (Gebäudetechnik, Facility Management, Unterhalt und Instandhaltung) inkl. Rollen, Prozessen, Ressourcen, Services und Einbezug von externen Anbietern unter dem Aspekt von zeitgemässen Arbeitsweisen unter Berücksichtigung der technologischen Möglichkeiten definieren
* Die verschiedenen Budgetpositionen bewirtschaften und ein Betriebsbudget erarbeiten
* Den dereinstigen Umzug von der heutigen JVA Thorberg in die neue JVA in Abstimmung mit den Nutzern planen und begleiten
* Innerhalb der strategischen Vorgaben die bauliche, technische und betriebliche Funktionstauglichkeit sowie die Werterhaltung der Objekte gewährleisten
* Übernahme von weiteren Infrastrukturprojekten der JVA Witzwil und des AJV
**Ihr Profil**
* Tertiärer Abschluss im Bereich Facility Management, Elektro- oder Gebäudetechnik (Ingenieur/-in, MAS in Real Estate und Facility Management, BSc Facility Management, Projektleiter/-in Gebäudeautomation mit eidg. Fachausweis, dipl. Gebäudetechniker/-in HF o.ä.)
* Umfangreiche Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Facility Management, Instandhaltung, HLKKSE, MSRL und BIM
* Ausgewiesene Erfahrung in der Durchführung von umfangreichen Neubauprojekten, der Führung von Projektmitarbeitenden sowie in der Bewirtschaftung von Budgetpositionen/Kostenstellen
* Erfahrung im Bereich Safety \& Security sowie dem Betrieb von besonders schützenswerten Infrastrukturen
* Motivierte, belastbare, selbstsichere und lösungsorientierte Persönlichkeit mit betriebswirtschaftlichem Verständnis, guten Umgangsformen, Durchsetzungsvermögen sowie Verhandlungsgeschick
* Ausgeprägte konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten sowie empfängergerechte Kommunikationsfähigkeit
* Visionäre und zukunftsgerichtete Denkweise verbunden mit Einfühlungsvermögen, um kritische Stimmen überzeugend zu begegnen.
* Flexibilität, bei Bedarf Einsätze auch ausserhalb der Bürozeiten auszuführen (Pikettdienst)
* Führerausweis der Kat. B

eine vielseitige und interessante Tätigkeit in einem lebhaften Betrieb, flexible Arbeitszeiten (Jahresarbeitszeitmodell) sowie der Möglichkeit, ab 2029 Einsitz in der GL einer modernen und schweizweit einzigartigen Vollzugseinrichtung zu nehmen mit der Verantwortung für ein sehr umfassendes und anspruchsvolles Infrastrukturportfolio.

Du leitest anspruchsvolle Infrastrukturprojekte von der Planung bis zur Umsetzung und gestaltest damit die Weiterentwicklung unserer Anlagen sowie Gebäude aktiv mit. * Du leitest von Infrastruktur- Projekte wie z.B. Erneuerungen verfahrenstechnischer Anlagen im Bereich der Abwasserreinigungsanlage (ARA), den Neubau eines Logistikstützpunkts oder Sanierungen / Umbauten der Gebäudeinfrastruktur.

* Du stellst die Einhaltung von gesetzlichen Vorschriften, Qualitätsanforderungen und gängiger Sicherheitsstandards sicher.

* Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Maschinenbau, Bauingenieurwesen, Wirtschaftsingenieurswesen, Verfahrenstechnik, Architektur oder ähnlicher Fachrichtung
* Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Leitung von Gross- oder Infrastrukturprojekten, idealerweise mit Berührungspunkten zum öffentlichen Sektor
* Fundierte Kenntnisse im Projektmanagement sowie idealerweise im Bau- und Vergaberecht
* Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Planungsbüros, Generalplanern und Lieferanten
* Verhandlungsgeschick, Durchsetzungsvermögen und diplomatisches Fingerspitzengefühl im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern

The Staff Technical Program Manager (TPM)- Devices resides within the Product and Technology organization and drives the end-to-end delivery of complex, cross-functional technical programs and strategic initiatives.

Working closely with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, and Operations teams, this leader drives alignment, mitigates risk, and delivers measurable business outcomes.

Drive end-to-end program execution from initiation through launch, ensuring stakeholder alignment across all milestones.
Coordinate cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Regulatory, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Operations.
Manage technical dependencies, risks, issues, and mitigation plans across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Facilitate technical discussions regarding architecture decisions, systems integration, platform scalability, and design tradeoffs.

Develop and maintain program dashboards, status reports, key performance indicators, and executive communications.
Apply Lean, Agile, Scrum, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies to deliver predictable outcomes.
Leverage AI-powered tools and automation to improve program reporting, risk identification, dashboard creation, and operational efficiency.
Establish and track program success metrics, ensuring measurable outcomes and transparent progress reporting.
Drive stakeholder communication, influence decision-making, and resolve blockers through collaboration and negotiation.
Conduct post-launch reviews and implement lessons learned to continuously improve delivery processes.
Mentor and develop junior Technical Program Managers, providing coaching on risk management, systems thinking, and program leadership.
Shape organizational processes and operating models while serving as a thought leader for the TPM function.

Proven ability to identify, manage, and mitigate program risks while balancing scope, schedule, cost, and quality.
Experience leveraging AI and automation tools to improve program management processes, reporting, and operational efficiency.
Strong communication, stakeholder management, and influence skills with the ability to work effectively across all organizational levels.

Experience leading hardware, firmware, and regulated medical device development programs from concept through launch.

Experience driving organizational process improvements and operating model transformations.

The Project Manager, State and Local Government is a five-year, fixed-term position supported by a contract with the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA). Employment is expected to continue for up to five years, subject to continued program funding, organizational needs, and performance.
Reporting to the Vice President, State and Local Government within the U.S. Market Transformation & Development team, you will serve as the lead project manager for a five-year statewide initiative supporting annual cohorts of New York local governments as they develop and implement ambitious clean energy and decarbonization strategies.
You will oversee the full lifecycle of multiple annual cohorts, ensuring successful program planning, implementation, stakeholder engagement, technical assistance delivery, curriculum development, partner coordination, contract compliance, and continuous program improvement.

Working closely with NYSERDA, local governments, subject matter experts, regional partners, universities, and internal cross-functional teams, you will help communities translate climate goals into measurable actions while supporting scalable and replicable approaches to market transformation.
This position serves as the primary day-to-day contact for NYSERDA and is responsible for ensuring exceptional program execution, strategic alignment, and delivery of all contractual commitments while advancing equitable, resilient, and high-performance communities throughout New York State.

Lead the planning and execution of a five-year, multi-cohort statewide program, managing the full lifecycle of annual cohorts of New York local governments from recruitment and onboarding through implementation, reporting, and closeout.
Serve as the primary project manager and day-to-day liaison for NYSERDA, ensuring contract compliance, timely delivery of milestones, budget oversight, reporting, risk management, and fulfillment of all program deliverables.
Manage cross-functional teams and external partners, including subject matter experts, subcontractors, regional organizations, universities, USGBC Chapters, and local government stakeholders to ensure coordinated program delivery and an exceptional participant experience.
Develop and oversee cohort curriculum, technical assistance, and participant resources, including orientations, workshops, learning sessions, implementation guides, playbooks, and other educational materials that support local government decarbonization efforts.
Provide strategic guidance and technical support to participating local governments, facilitating workshops, office hours, peer learning, and one-on-one coaching to help communities develop and implement clean energy and climate action strategies.
Establish and maintain strong project governance practices, including project plans, schedules, budgets, risk logs, performance metrics, documentation, and continuous process improvements to ensure successful program execution.
Lead stakeholder engagement and external communications, representing USGBC at meetings, conferences, webinars, and public events while coordinating dissemination of best practices, lessons learned, and market transformation resources.
Supervise program staff, fellows, interns, and consultants, fostering collaboration, accountability, and high-quality execution while supporting the strategic goals of USGBC and NYSERDA.

Experience coordinating cross-functional teams, external partners, and government stakeholders.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

We're looking for a technology program manager to own the technical needs that follow our executives outside the four walls of the enterprise: their homes, their vehicles, and their travel. Reporting to the Protective Services Lead, this role sits at the intersection of physical security technology, hands-on program delivery, and vendor management.

The Engineering & Technology Lead sets the architecture and strategic plan for security technology across GSIS; you'll own execution for the personal and residential slice of that footprint, the systems that protect executives and their families wherever they actually are, not just at the office.
This is not a coordination-only role.

You'll need enough technical fluency to make good calls on the ground without waiting for architecture sign-off on every decision, enough program rigor to keep vendors and installs on track, and enough judgment to know when something belongs back with the Protective Services Lead because it touches strategy or standards beyond your scope.

Much of the documentation you produce will be read by people who never see the systems themselves, so clarity matters as much as technical correctness.

Own residential security system design, integration, and lifecycle management for assigned executive residences (cameras, alarms, access control, sensor networks), aligned to the standards set by the Protective Services Lead
Own home network design and hardening for executive residences and travel, coordinating with corporate IT/InfoSec standards where they intersect
Manage the technology side of travel security: secure communications provisioning, single-use travel hardware, and rapid-deployment kits for new or temporary properties
Manage the vendor relationships and contracts for the residential and personal technology stack, installers, monitoring providers, communications providers, within the governance framework the Protective Service Lead sets
Maintain system health monitoring, managed maintenance, and as-built documentation for technology deployed outside the enterprise perimeter
Own decommissioning and transition of technology when properties or vehicles change, so nothing orphaned (access, data, or hardware) gets left behind
Act as first point of contact and triage for executive and family requests involving personal technology and security systems, resolving directly where you can and routing to the Protective Services Lead when it requires a broader architecture or strategy decision
Contribute audit-ready documentation for the technology under your ownership to support regulatory, customer, and partner diligence requests
You may be a good fit if you
Bring hands-on physical security technology experience from residential, travel, or personal-protection contexts, not only corporate/enterprise systems
Have solid program management experience delivering security technology, you know what a well-run install, vendor relationship, or rapid deployment actually looks like
Have contributed to or led the build of security technology capabilities from zero in a high-growth environment, including documentation, playbooks, and training
Can manage vendor relationships through a full lifecycle: selection, contracting, onboarding, performance management, and renewal
Write clearly and can translate technical tradeoffs for audiences that range from engineers to principals to household staff
Are comfortable operating with moderate ambiguity, and know when a decision is yours to make versus one that belongs with whoever owns the broader technology strategy
Care about Anthropic's mission and the unique security considerations that come with building frontier AI systems

Have 10+ years of experience delivering physical security technology programs
Have direct experience with residential or executive-protection-adjacent technology deployments specifically, not just corporate office systems
Have worked at an AI-focused organization, frontier technology company, or similarly high-growth, high-scrutiny environment
Have managed distributed vendor networks across multiple properties or regions

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. # Projektleiter/in Technik / Industrie (m/w) #
In dieser vielseitigen und verantwortungsvollen Funktion übernehmen Sie die selbstständige Planung, Koordination und Betreuung anspruchsvoller technischer Projekte und begleiten diese von der Anfrage bis zur erfolgreichen Umsetzung bzw. Serienreife.

Sie koordinieren die verschiedenen internen und externen Schnittstellen, überwachen Termine, Kosten sowie Projektfortschritte und stellen eine strukturierte und zielgerichtete Projektabwicklung sicher. Dabei arbeiten Sie eng mit Kunden sowie den Bereichen Entwicklung, Produktion, Qualität, Einkauf und weiteren Fachstellen zusammen.

Technische Abklärungen, das Erkennen möglicher Projektrisiken und die Einleitung entsprechender Massnahmen sowie eine transparente Projektdokumentation und ein regelmässiges Reporting gehören ebenfalls zu Ihrem abwechslungsreichen Aufgabengebiet.
Sie verfügen über eine abgeschlossene technische Grundausbildung, beispielsweise als Polymechaniker, Konstrukteur, Anlagen- und Apparatebauer, Kunststofftechnologe oder in einem vergleichbaren Beruf.

Idealerweise haben Sie sich technisch, betriebswirtschaftlich oder im Bereich Projektmanagement weitergebildet und konnten bereits Erfahrung in einem industriellen bzw. produzierenden Umfeld sammeln. Erfahrung in der Leitung oder Koordination technischer Projekte ist von Vorteil.

Gerne berücksichtigen wir auch ambitionierte technische Fach- oder Führungskräfte, welche den nächsten Karriereschritt in Richtung Projektleitung anstreben. Sie besitzen ein gutes Verständnis für technische und betriebliche Zusammenhänge und überzeugen mit einer selbstständigen, strukturierten und lösungsorientierten Arbeitsweise.

Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sowie gute IT-Anwenderkenntnisse runden Ihr Profil ab.

Wir sind seit über 130 Jahren Teil der Region Zug \- und voller Energie für das, was kommt. Stillstand kennen wir nicht. Du möchtest komplexe Arealprojekte koordinieren, unterschiedliche Fachbereiche zusammenbringen und die Energiezukunft aktiv mitgestalten? Dann steig bei uns ein.
Bei WWZ entwickeln wir nachhaltige und vernetzte Energielösungen. Für unsere anspruchsvollen Areal\- und Inf\-rastrukturprojekte suchen wir eine engagierte Persönlichkeit, die den Überblick behält, Schnittstellen aktiv gestal\-tet und technische, administrative sowie vertragliche Themen sicher zusammenführt.
Deine Aufgaben
In dieser vielseitigen Funktion übernimmst du die Gesamtkoordination von Arealprojekten für externe Kundinnen und Kunden. Du sorgst dafür, dass alle Beteiligten effizient zusammenarbeiten und die Projekte entlang des ge\-samten Lebenszyklus erfolgreich vorankommen.
\- Du koordinierst Arealprojekte in den Themenfeldern Energieversorgung, Wärme und Kälte, E\-Mobilität, ZEV, LEG, Photovoltaik, Batteriespeicher, Netznutzung, Gas und Bau.
\- Du verbindest interne Fachbereiche mit externen Kundinnen und Kunden sowie Partnerunternehmen und stellst einen reibungslosen Informationsfluss sicher.
\- Du erstellst und pflegst Dienstleistungsverträge und behältst Fristen, Leistungen sowie Vereinbarungen im Blick.
\- Du begleitest Angebots\-, Rechnungs\- und Inkassoprozesse und sorgst für klare und verlässliche Abläufe.
\- Du erkennst Herausforderungen an den Schnittstellen zwischen Technik, Betrieb und Administration und entwickelst pragmatische Lösungen.
\- Du treibst die Standardisierung, Digitalisierung und Automatisierung unserer Prozesse voran \- insbeson\-dere im Datenmanagement, Vertragswesen und in der Abrechnung.
\- Du unterstützt die Projektleitungen, verantwortest eigene Teilprojekte und bringst deine Ideen in die Weiterentwicklung unserer Dienstleistungen ein.
Das bringst du mit
Du verfügst über eine abgeschlossene technische Grundausbildung, idealerweise in der Elektro\-, Energie\- oder Versorgungstechnik. Eine Weiterbildung auf Stufe HF oder FH ergänzt dein Profil.

\- mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in der Energiebranche, beispielsweise im Umfeld von Areallösungen, Ener\-gieversorgung, Gebäudetechnik oder Immobilienmanagement
\- Erfahrung in der Koordination komplexer technischer Projekte und in der Zusammenarbeit mit interdis\-ziplinären Teams
\- Verständnis für Gesamtenergielösungen, Vertrags\- und Abrechnungsmanagement sowie energiewirt\-schaftliche Zusammenhänge
\- betriebswirtschaftliches Denken und Erfahrung im Umgang mit Kosten, Budgets und Prozessen
\- Freude an Digitalisierung, Datenqualität und Prozessoptimierung
\- sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse; Englischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil
Du denkst vernetzt, arbeitest strukturiert und behältst auch bei komplexen Projekten den Überblick. Im Austausch mit unterschiedlichen Anspruchsgruppen trittst du sicher auf, kommunizierst klar und findest gemeinsam mit an\-deren tragfähige Lösungen. Es erwarten dich anspruchsvolle und abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben in einem zukunftsgerichteten, lebendigen Unternehmen.
Du darfst mit viel Teamspirit, fortschrittlichen Anstellungsbedingungen und einem attraktiven Arbeitsplatz mit moderner Infrastruktur rechnen.
Bei uns gestaltest du mit und entwickelst nicht nur deine Projekte, sondern auch dich selbst – wir unterstützen und fördern dich dabei.

You'll own Replit's disputes and chargeback function end-to-end: from the individual case in front of you to the policies, playbooks, and automation that let it hold up as we scale to millions of users. This role combines strategic ownership with hands-on execution: you'll determine dispute and chargeback strategy, and build the systems that make those decisions repeatable at scale, working closely with Engineering, Legal and Finance.
In this role you will…
Own the full dispute lifecycle: investigate incoming chargebacks and disputes, decide whether and how to represent, gather evidence, and respond within network deadlines.
Design and maintain the policies, decision trees, and SOPs that govern how disputes and chargebacks are handled.
Define the key metrics, health targets, and goals for the disputes program and track performance against them, reporting to leadership.
Monitor chargeback rates and dispute trends to identify the underlying drivers of volume, and partner with Engineering and Finance to address root causes.
Partner with Engineering and Support Operations to automate manual parts of the workflow (evidence gathering, decisioning logic, etc).
Build training, documentation, and escalation paths that enable frontline support teams to handle dispute-related inquiries confidently and consistently as the program scales.

6+ years of hands-on experience owning disputes/chargebacks operations, ideally where you built or significantly leveled up the function rather than just running an existing one.
Deep familiarity with major card network dispute rules and reason codes (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover), including compelling-evidence frameworks and network monitoring/excessive-dispute programs (e.g., Visa's VDMP/VFMP, Mastercard's ECP)
Experience building or improving SOPs, playbooks, or workflows in a support or operations environment.
Experience partnering with Engineering to scope and prioritize automation, even if you're not writing the code yourself.
Comfort operating as both a hands-on operator and systems builder in a scaling environment.
Strong judgment and decision-making skills when handling sensitive or ambiguous customer situations.
Experience translating policy or legal requirements into clear, repeatable processes or customer-facing guidance.
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly, empathetically, and precisely in high-stakes situations.
Proven track record working cross-functionally to deliver impactful results.

Hands-on experience with Stripe's dispute tooling specifically, including submitting evidence and managing dispute workflows through Stripe.
Experience in customer support, trust & safety, support operations, or similar roles within a technology company.
Experience in a high-growth or usage-based SaaS environment, where dispute patterns and volume can shift quickly with product changes.
Familiarity with fraud detection tooling and how it intersects with the disputes function.
Experience managing outsourced or contract support as programs scale, in case this function grows beyond a single person down the line.

About Supabase
Supabase is the open-source backend platform trusted by millions of developers to build web apps, SaaS products, and AI-native applications. Our Partnerships team works across the ecosystem - technology partners, cloud platforms, VCs, accelerators, and startup programs - to make Supabase the default backend for the next generation of companies.

We're looking for a Startup Partner Enablement & Programs Manager to bring our partner ecosystem to life through enablement, events, and programs to raise awareness of Supabase's value proposition to early stage startups.

You'll own the materials, playbooks, and activations that help our partners - VCs, accelerators, incubators and entrepreneurship programs - successfully promote and build with Supabase.

That includes organizing Supabase's presence at partner and VC-related events, running office hours, hackathons and VIP dinners, and turning relationships into repeatable, high-impact programs.
This role sits on the Partnerships team and reports to the Head of Startups, working closely with teammates across the startup program, GTM, developer relations, and marketing.

Because the bulk of our events and partner activity is concentrated in San Francisco and the Bay Area, we strongly prefer candidates based there who can regularly attend and host events in person.

It's a great fit for someone who loves the operational craft of enablement and programs and wants to work at the intersection of startups, venture, and developer tools.

Build and maintain partner enablement materials - decks, one-pagers, playbooks, and activation guides - that help partners across the ecosystem promote and build with Supabase
Manage the operational cadence of partner programs: collaborating on strategy, tracking activations, and keeping program logistics running smoothly across partner types
Organize Supabase's presence at partner and VC-related events — demo days, founder summits, portfolio workshops, partner conferences — including sourcing and preparing speakers for talks and panels
Plan and run Supabase hackathons end-to-end: partner coordination, logistics, sponsorships, judging, prizes, promotion, and post-event follow-through
Coordinate cross-functionally with the Partnerships, Startups, GTM, DevRel, Events and Marketing teams to align enablement and event activity with pipeline goals
Measure and report on program impact — signups, credit redemptions, partner-sourced pipeline, and event outcomes
Identify new enablement and program opportunities across the partner ecosystem and bring proposals with clear ROI to the team

Cognite operates at the forefront of industrial digitalization, building AI , and data solutions that solve the world’s hardest, highest-impact problems. With unmatched industrial heritage and a comprehensive suite of AI capabilities, including low-code AI agents, Cognite accelerates the digital transformation to drive operational improvements.
We thrive in challenges. We challenge assumptions. We execute with speed and ownership. If you view obstacles as signals to step forward - not backwards - you’ll feel right at home here.
Our Moonshot is bold: Unlock $100B in customer value by 2035, and redefine how global industry works. Join us in this venture where AI and data meet ingenuity, and together, we will forge the path to a smarter, more connected industrial future.
How you’ll demonstrate Ownership
As a Co-Innovation Program Manager, you'll drive the programs that turn Cognite's emerging capabilities into production-ready product. You'll work at the seam between product development and customer reality—using real-world deployments to harden new features, identify gaps, and systematically improve the platform, systems, and processes.

You orchestrate across engineers, product managers, designers, and customer teams to keep complex programs on track and ensure learnings flow back into the product roadmap.

Drive Co-Innovation: Own end-to-end delivery of customer-partnered programs, managing scope, timelines, resources, and risks.

Klaviyo's infrastructure is the foundation that every product, every customer, and every engineer depends on. In this role you will be the connective tissue between our Infrastructure organization and the rest of engineering, driving the rollout of critical, cross-cutting programs that affect how we build, operate, and secure our platform at scale.
You will juggle a high volume of parallel efforts across cloud infrastructure, FinOps, build systems, software migrations, security operations, and more, keeping each moving, supporting teams to be successful, and escalating quickly when capacity or priority decisions need to be made. This is not a role for someone who waits to be told what to do. It's a role for someone who drives.
How you'll make a difference
Own the rollout of infrastructure initiatives across engineering. Drive programs from planning through completion, coordinating across teams that don't report to you and don't always have capacity to prioritize infrastructure work. Keep things moving.
Manage a high volume of concurrent efforts. At any given time you'll be tracking security operations improvements, FinOps initiatives, build system changes, software migrations, and other cross-cutting infrastructure programs simultaneously. Clear prioritization and status visibility are non-negotiable.
Hold teams accountable and escalate when needed. You know how to build the relationships and create the visibility that keeps infrastructure work from getting deprioritized. When a team genuinely lacks capacity, you surface that quickly, bring the right people into the conversation, and get a trade-off decision made — not absorb the delay quietly.
Develop a way to provide program health continuously. Establish and maintain clear, actionable reporting on the status of all infrastructure rollouts. Leadership should always know what's on track, what's at risk, and what decisions are needed from them.
Partner with Infrastructure leadership on planning and prioritization. Work closely with engineering and SRE leadership to build and maintain a rolling roadmap, sequence work across teams, and ensure infrastructure investments align with engineering and business priorities.
Define clear ways of working across teams. Create frameworks, templates, and coordination models that make it easier for infrastructure and product engineering teams to work together effectively. Build the playbook as you go.
Develop deep technical fluency in the programs you own. You don't need to write the code, but you need to understand what's being built, why it matters, and what the technical risks are well enough to ask the right questions, identify blockers early, and represent the work credibly to engineering leadership.
Drive automation and operational excellence. Challenge manual processes wherever you find them. Partner with infrastructure teams to identify opportunities to centralize and automate change rather than default to simply assigning out the same work to different teams.

Technically fluent. You've worked closely with infrastructure, SRE, or platform engineering teams. You understand security operations, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and software migrations well enough to engage substantively, not just track status.
A driver, not a facilitator. You move work forward. You follow up, push back, escalate, and hold people accountable, constructively, but consistently. You don't wait for the next meeting to surface a problem.
Influential and relationship-driven. You know that infrastructure work gets done through trust, not authority. You build strong relationships across engineering teams, understand what motivates different stakeholders, and use that context to create alignment
AI-first in how you work. You don't just talk about AI, you use it daily to move faster, work smarter, and do more with less. You bring that mindset to the teams you work with and actively look for opportunities to automate, accelerate, and improve how programs are run.
Comfortable with high volume and ambiguity. You can manage many parallel workstreams without losing track of any of them, and you don't need a clean problem statement to get started.
Clear and direct communicator. You tailor your message by audience, engineering teams need different information than engineering VPs, and you make it easy for leadership to understand status and make decisions quickly.
Outcome-oriented. You measure success by realizing the impact and what improves, not by the quality of your tracking.

8+ years of experience in technical program management within a fast-paced product engineering environment, ideally SaaS or high-growth tech.
Demonstrated experience driving large-scale infrastructure rollouts across multiple engineering teams.
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, FinOps, security operations, and software migration programs.
Strong fluency in tools such as Jira, Linear, Asana, or Smartsheet.
Track record of managing competing priorities and delivering results without direct authority over engineering teams.

Familiarity with FinOps frameworks and cloud cost optimization programs.
Experience building or evolving TPM practices in a nascent or growing function.
Hands-on with CI/CD tooling, build systems, or security compliance frameworks.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Project Manager to lead two connected migration workstreams within a complex enterprise technology program. This is not a generic coordination role. You will provide hands-on delivery leadership across technically complex, security-sensitive migrations, creating clarity from partially defined requirements and driving the program through planning, dependency management, operational readiness, execution, and closure.
The role requires close coordination between business, engineering, security, identity, infrastructure, and enabling platform teams. You will be expected to challenge weak plans, surface risks early, drive decisions, and keep senior stakeholders aligned around facts, trade-offs, and clear next actions.
The two workstreams focus on reducing technology risk and modernizing access and identity capabilities. One involves migrating external users from unmanaged BYOD access toward managed devices or VDI-based access through AWS. The second involves migrating legacy identity configurations onto a standardized Entra ID setup within existing Active Directory environments.

translate the migration objectives into an executable program structure with clear workstreams, milestones, owners, assumptions, and success criteria,
define clear scope and accountability across engineering, security, identity, infrastructure, O365 administration, and business stakeholders,
create and maintain an integrated roadmap, identify the critical path, and highlight areas requiring additional staffing, technical decisions, or leadership support,
own the integrated delivery plan from current-state analysis through migration design, execution readiness, rollout, and closure,
coordinate participating teams and external contributors to ensure workstreams remain aligned and dependencies are actively managed,
ensure migrations include business readiness, stakeholder communications, cutover planning, fallback considerations, and post-migration validation,
maintain a transparent view of risks, actions, issues, dependencies, and decisions across the migration workstreams,
identify and escalate delivery blockers early, particularly around device strategy, regional rollout constraints, identity dependencies, tenant configuration, and capacity,
escalate issues with clear recommendations and drive them through to resolution,
establish lightweight but rigorous governance appropriate for a security-sensitive migration program,
maintain the integrated plan, RAID log, dependency map, decision log, stakeholder map, and executive status reporting,
establish migration-readiness checkpoints and ensure teams are prepared for controlled execution,
challenge technical plans and migration sequencing where hidden dependencies or delivery risks exist,
facilitate productive discussions between identity, endpoint, infrastructure, security, and engineering specialists,
translate technical constraints and dependencies into clear business and program implications,
provide concise, fact-based reporting to senior stakeholders, clearly distinguishing progress, risks, blockers, and required decisions,
ensure program governance remains focused on decision-making and delivery discipline rather than unnecessary administrative overhead,

The first things you'd own
We think in rocks, meaning the things that need pushing uphill. Here are ours, in priority order.
1. Capacity planning. Right now we don't have a real model for who is working on what, how loaded they are, or what happens when a new account lands. You'd build it: a live view of capacity across media buyers, designers, and video editors, with the ability to see an overload coming two weeks out instead of the day someone misses a deadline.
2. Creative workflow and process. Creative is our biggest bottleneck and it's cross functional. It spans our graphic design team, our video editors, and our media buyers who double as creative strategists. There's no single pipeline from request to delivery right now. You'd build it, run it, and be the person who guarantees we hit the creative volumes we owe clients every month.
3. Creators and UGC. We source creators constantly and there's no system behind it. You'd own sourcing across Billo, Backstage, email, and wherever else the right person is. That means negotiating rates and turnaround, tracking orders, managing usage rights so we never run an ad we've lost the rights to, tracking costs per account, and making sure markups land correctly on client invoices. If you haven't done this before, you should be genuinely comfortable asking a stranger for a better rate.
4. Client onboarding. We have a process and it needs refining, by someone who does this for a living rather than by me. Account access collection (Meta Business Manager, Google Ads, Klaviyo, Shopify, TikTok), ClickUp setup, reporting and dashboard configuration, so every launch feels identical.
What you'd do day to day
Run ClickUp as the single source of truth. Build and maintain templates, recurring tasks, intake forms, automations, and dashboards. Every account has a current status and a named owner, always.
Own capacity planning across the paid media team and flag overload before it becomes a missed deliverable.
Track every creative deliverable from request to delivery, including revisions and approvals, and QA the work before it reaches a client.
Source, negotiate with, and manage creators. Track orders, usage rights, and costs.
Own client onboarding end to end and standardize it so every launch runs the same way.
Build landing pages and advertorials using Claude Code from time to time.
Make sure client reporting and dashboards are set up correctly and stay accurate for every account.
Build internal tools, automations, and living SOPs using AI so the whole team runs faster and the same way every time.
Catch gaps in communication and delivery before they escalate, and drive follow ups to closure.
Schedule and coordinate recurring client and internal meetings, capture action items, and make sure they actually get done.
Flag at risk accounts early and escalate.
About the landing pages
We don't sell landing pages as a service. We build them anyway, because a weak page is the most common reason good creative doesn't convert, and waiting on a client's dev team costs us weeks.
Our media buyers already build pages this way. You'd do the same: advertorials, presell pages, and landing page variants built with Claude Code off existing templates and shipped to Shopify or the client's stack. You don't need to be an engineer and you won't be architecting anything from scratch. You need to be someone who can take a brief, work with AI to build the page, QA it, and ship it, and who finds that interesting rather than terrifying.
How we work, and please read this part carefully
This is the part most job posts leave out, and it's the part that actually determines whether you'd be happy here.
We give a lot of autonomy and we mean it. Nobody here is on a time clock and nobody ever will be. If I have to think about what you're doing with your hours, we've already lost. I judge outcomes, not activity.
The flip side is that I'm not a gatekeeper. One of the biggest red flags for me is someone who asks a lot of permission questions. Can I change this, should I do that. No. Just do it and show me. If you need a company card to solve something, you'll have one. You have full trust on day one. It's only ever lost, never earned.
Ownership is the thing we care about most. "That wasn't my role" is a disqualifier here. If creative is the bottleneck on an account, you go fix creative, whether or not it was in your scope. We've all done work outside our lane to get the result.
We judge the first 30 days harshly. We're looking for you to take action early and show that you're self directed. We usually know quickly, and it rarely turns around. What I can tell you is that people who make it past that point almost never leave. Our team retention is exceptional.
Mistakes are fine. Patterns aren't. You'll never hear me raise my voice. When something breaks we look at the process, not the person. My Slack tagline is "everything's my fault." But if the same thing breaks repeatedly, that's a fit problem.
My job is to protect the team. We have let go of clients for being unkind to our people and we'll do it again. I ask you to put clients first, and if there's ever a problem, tell me, because I'll put you first.
I like being wrong. Tell me there's a better way. Nothing here is sacred and everything can change.
Where this goes
On our email side, project management became the pipeline into strategy. Several of our email strategists started as PMs. We're building the same path on paid media. If you want to end up as a media buyer or creative strategist, this is the seat that gets you there, and you'll get your hands dirty along the way, writing creative briefs, launching ads, and sitting in on account reviews.
If you'd rather stay in operations and own this function as it grows, that works too. Tell us which one you want.
Our mission is simple: be the no BS agency partner you love working with.

Localisation efforts at Klaviyo are centred around linguistic excellence, teamwork and scale. Manage all localisation for Product, Help Centre and Customer Education , partnering closely with those teams to deliver high quality, locally relevant experiences across all supported languages.
Manage all language contractors (including freelance linguists, agencies and other language vendors), ensuring we have the right resourcing, quality, cost and workflows in place to support current and future localisation needs.

End-to-end localisation ownership for Product, Help Centre and Customer Education : Plan, execute and manage localisation solutions for the Klaviyo Product, Help Centre and Customer Education teams, partnering closely with those teams to fully understand business goals, priorities and opportunities.

Language quality management : Define clear expectations and quality standards for all languages, set up scalable review and feedback loops, and manage performance to ensure we meet or exceed quality, timeliness and cost targets. Own and manage the Klaviyo Language hub (language governance) and associated processes across all languages.
TMS and MT ownership : Own and manage our TMS (Smartling) as it relates to Product, Help Centre and Customer Education, ensuring optimisation for different content types, CMSs, language assets and resources, and integrating and managing machine translation within our workflows for all supported languages.
AI-first translation platform : Partner with Engineering, Product, Data and other internal teams to help design and build an AI-first translation platform that leverages MT, generative AI and automation to increase localisation speed, consistency and scalability while maintaining quality.
Transform workflows by putting AI at the centre, building smarter systems and ways of working from the ground up.
Collaboration across the Localisation team : Collaborate with the broader Localisation team to deliver a high-quality localised experience for international customers, drive scale in localisation, and resolve issues and blockers quickly.
Champion the international customer : Be a champion internally for the international Klaviyo customer, ensuring their needs are represented in content, product decisions and localisation priorities.

Qui sommes\-nous ?
Alpenda est un acteur de référence de la construction en Suisse romande depuis plus de 100 ans.

Forte de près de 200 collaborateurs, l'entreprise accompagne ses clients dans leurs projets de construction et de rénovation grâce à une approche globale couvrant la conception, la planification, la réalisation et la modernisation des bâtiments, avec une attention particulière portée à la qualité, à l'innovation et à la durabilité.

Filiale suisse du groupe DEMATHIEU BARD, Alpenda poursuit le développement de projets d'envergure. Ce lien renforce les synergies et les expertises des deux entreprises tout en préservant l'identité, la proximité et l'ancrage local qui font la force d'Alpenda.

Vous rejoignez la Direction Exploitation, en charge du pilotage des chantiers de l'ensemble des projets d'Alpenda. Sa mission est de garantir un haut niveau d'exigence en matière de qualité, de sécurité, de respect de l'environnement, ainsi que de maîtrise des délais et des budgets.

Nos équipes spécialisées interviennent sur des projets variés, en construction neuve comme en rénovation, dans les secteurs résidentiel et fonctionnel.

Reconnus pour notre expertise dans la réalisation de projets haut de gamme, nous accordons une importance particulière à l'accompagnement de nos clients, à la transparence de nos échanges et à l'excellence de nos prestations. En tant que Chef de Projet, vous assurez la gestion technique et le bon déroulement du projet.

Vous veillez également à la bonne représentation de l’entreprise et êtes un véritable leader de terrain, reconnu pour votre polyvalence et votre capacité à fédérer les différents intervenants.
Chef de projet H/F

Vous entretenez et développez les relations avec le Maître d’Ouvrage, les mandataires, les entreprises et les autorités
Vous analysez les appels d’offres, comparez les soumissions et pilotez le processus d’adjudication. Vous accompagnez les équipes dans les négociations avec les entreprises et les partenaires

Vous assurez le suivi financier du projet, notamment la gestion budgétaire, le contrôle des coûts, la validation des situations de paiement et l’établissement du décompte final
Pourquoi pas vous ?
Vous avez obtenu un diplôme d’architecte ETS, HES ou EPF, de dessinateur en bâtiment ou en génie civil, d’ingénieur du bâtiment ou un titre jugé équivalent ?
Vous avez bénéficié d’une formation dans la conduite de travaux ou la gestion de projet ?
Vous justifiez d’au minimum 5 ans d’expérience en tant que Chef de Projet, idéalement au sein d’une Entreprise Totale ou Générale ?
Vous bénéficiez d’une première expérience réussie en Suisse dans une fonction similaire ?
Vous possédez de solides connaissances techniques, financières, de planification et de contrôle qualité acquises au travers de vos expériences ?
Votre capacité à fédérer, coordonner et accompagner les équipes est reconnue ?
Votre expérience en gestion contractuelle, en négociation avec les entreprises et partenaires, ainsi qu’en pilotage des appels d’offres constitue un véritable atout ?

We are looking for a Technical Project Manager to join our product team. The Technical Project Manager is responsible for driving the successful execution of technical projects and initiatives, from planning through delivery.

They work closely with Product, Engineering, and other cross-functional teams to translate business and product priorities into actionable engineering plans, ensuring development resources are focused on the highest-priority initiatives.

The Technical Project Manager maintains project visibility, manages dependencies and timelines, identifies and resolves blockers, and proactively surfaces risks to stakeholders.

They also work directly with external partners and stakeholders to understand requirements, coordinate technical deliverables, and ensure successful execution across organizational boundaries.

The Technical Project Manager facilitates technical discussions and decision-making, adapting project plans as priorities shift to ensure teams remain aligned and projects are delivered effectively. To work at Talkspace, you need to be as passionate as we are about our work, and excited to partner with us on delivering quality mental healthcare.
This is a remote position based on Eastern Time. Talkspace Headquarters is located in NYC.

Technical Project Management
Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to translate roadmap priorities into executable engineering plans and ensure development resources are aligned to the highest-priority initiatives.
Lead the planning and execution of technical projects across the software development life cycle, from requirements through deployment.
Develop and maintain project timelines, milestones, and delivery plans, adjusting priorities and plans as business and technical needs evolve.
Track dependencies across multiple engineering workstreams and proactively identify and resolve conflicts or blockers.
Coordinate releases and technical initiatives across web, mobile, API, backend, and other engineering teams.
Monitor project health using quantitative metrics and qualitative signals, surfacing risks and opportunities to leadership early.
Maintain project documentation and visibility to ensure stakeholders have a clear understanding of project status, decisions, risks, and next steps.
Engineering Collaboration
Work closely with engineers and engineering leaders to unblock teams, facilitate decision-making, and ensure technical work remains aligned with product and business priorities.
Facilitate technical discussions and drive clarity and alignment when teams encounter complex decisions or competing priorities.
Coordinate sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, and other project ceremonies to support effective engineering execution.
Understand the software development life cycle and technical dependencies well enough to identify potential risks and help teams navigate challenges.
Adapt project management processes and methodologies to maximize team productivity and effectiveness in a fast-moving environment.
External Partner & Stakeholder Management
Serve as a key technical point of contact for external partners, customers, and other stakeholders, ensuring clear communication and alignment throughout project execution.
Gather and translate external partner requirements into actionable technical requirements, project plans, and priorities for internal teams.
Coordinate technical deliverables, integrations, timelines, and dependencies across internal engineering teams and external organizations.
Manage competing priorities and expectations across internal and external stakeholders, proactively identifying tradeoffs and escalating issues when needed.
Build strong relationships with external partners and stakeholders to facilitate collaboration, resolve issues, and ensure successful delivery of technical initiatives.
Communicate project status, risks, dependencies, and technical decisions to external stakeholders in a clear and accessible manner.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Design, Data, and other cross-functional teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
Translate technical information and project status into clear, actionable updates for non-technical stakeholders.
Partner with Product Management to understand business and user priorities and ensure engineering execution supports broader product strategy.
Collaborate with leadership to identify opportunities to improve engineering processes, resource allocation, and project execution.

5+ years of technical project management experience, ideally in a high-velocity technology or startup environment.
Strong understanding of the software development life cycle, from requirements gathering through deployment.
Experience coordinating complex projects across multiple engineering teams, technical workstreams, and external stakeholders.
Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proactive problem-solver who identifies risks, dependencies, and blockers before they impact project delivery.
Collaborative leader who builds trust through strong judgment, accountability, and follow-through.
Comfortable participating in technical discussions and working closely with engineers and engineering leadership.
Experience managing external partners, vendors, customers, or other stakeholders through complex technical projects.
Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies and the ability to adapt processes based on team and project needs.

Healthcare experience, particularly in regulated environments.
Experience working with healthcare providers, payers, EHRs, or other healthcare technology partners.
Familiarity with HIPAA compliance requirements and healthcare software development.
Experience with API, platform, or backend engineering projects.
Experience with tools such as Jira, Linear, GitHub, or similar project management platforms.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

Service Delivery is the backbone of ServiceNow's customer success strategy in the Americas. We manage the governance, performance, and strategic alignment of our global system integrator (SI) and service delivery partners ensuring that partner-delivered services meet the highest standards of quality, customer satisfaction, and business outcomes.

The Service Delivery function spans partner capacity planning, contingent worker onboarding, contract management, resource optimization, and end-to-end delivery governance across a large ecosystem of delivery partners serving thousands of customers.
As a Service Delivery Manager, you will be part of a team supporting the Director, Service Delivery in executing the regional service delivery strategy and governance frameworks. Your focus will be on the tactical, day-to-day oversight and governance of assigned partner engagements, ensuring consistent execution of ServiceNow standards, quality metrics, and customer outcomes.

The Service Delivery Manager is responsible for overseeing the performance, quality, and operational health of assigned partners. Acting as the primary governance point between ServiceNow and delivery partner(s) for your assigned portfolio, you ensure partner resources assigned to ServiceNow engagements are delivered in accordance with agreed service levels, quality standards, contractual commitments, and customer outcome expectations.
You monitor service delivery performance, identify risks, drive corrective actions, manage escalations, and provide ongoing visibility into delivery health for leadership.

Your role serves as the critical accountability layer that makes partner performance predictable, scalable, and aligned to ServiceNow standards across your assigned partners, regardless of whether they are delivering managed services, outsourced operations, subcontracted services, or project-based engagements.

You work closely with the Director, Service Delivery to implement governance processes, contribute to strategic initiatives, and escalate systemic issues that require regional leadership attention.

Partner Performance Governance
Serve as the primary ServiceNow point of contact for assigned partner points of contact; maintaining day-to-day oversight of partner service performance against contracted KPIs and SLAs.
Monitor service delivery performance across assigned partners, tracking key metrics including quality scores, customer satisfaction, utilization rates, delivery timelines, and cost-per-outcome performance; ensuring that ServiceNow and its customers are getting excellence in delivery from its partner resources.
Review delivery quality trends, audit findings, and operational metrics to identify systemic issues, root causes, and opportunities for continuous improvement within assigned portfolio.
Monitor delivery unit economics and cost-per-outcome performance, ensuring the contracted commercial model (unit-based, outcome-based, or hybrid) tracks to delivered value and flag discrepancies.
Maintain a dashboard or reporting view of assigned partner health metrics and escalate systemic issues to the Director, Service Delivery for strategic resolution or cross-regional alignment.
Escalation & Corrective Action
